# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Mute holds the manual and can read the rule, but Mute cannot speak — only gesture. Deaf can see gestures but I cannot. So the rule must travel: Mute gestures it to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I can reach the bomb and cut wires. I need the manual's rule. Please gesture it to Deaf, who can then speak it to me, since I cannot see gestures.")

```

My speak reached nobody — I must have misaddressed it. Let me reconsider the channels.

So my speech goes to Mute only. My gestures go to Deaf and Mute.

So I cannot speak to Deaf at all. Deaf receives my gestures only. But Deaf can't interpret gestures without a code. And I never receive gestures.

So the chain is: Mute (manual) gestures rule → Deaf sees gestures, and I... can't see them. Deaf speaks rule → who hears Deaf? Deaf speaks, and speech reaches those who can hear. Mute cannot hear (Deaf is the one who can't hear... wait).

Let me re-read the monkeys:
- Deaf: can see the bomb, cannot hear, cannot touch.
- Mute: can read the manual, cannot speak, cannot touch.
- Blind: can touch, cannot see.

So Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak. Blind (me) can speak and hear? I can speak (to Mute) and... I receive speech? The turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. "Whoever comes before you is already heard by the time you are asked." I come after Mute. So I hear Mute? But Mute cannot speak. Mute gestures.

Hmm, but I don't receive gestures ("You never receive gesture"). So Mute's gestures reach Deaf and Mute... no, gestures reach those who can see: Deaf and Blind? No — "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's *my* gesture reaching Deaf and Mute. Wait that says Mute receives my gesture, but Mute can't see either? Mute can read the manual — reading is visual. Actually Mute "cannot speak" but presumably can see.

Let me just use the stated channels for me:
- My speak → Mute.
- My gesture → Deaf and Mute.

And I receive: speech from those before me (Mute, but Mute can't speak). Deaf comes after me, so Deaf's speech reaches me next turn. Deaf can speak (Deaf can't hear but can speak). So Deaf speaks → I hear it next turn. Good, that's how Deaf's messages reach me.

So the relay: Mute gestures rule → Deaf sees it. Deaf speaks rule → I hear it next turn. That works.

But my speak to Deaf failed because my speak only reaches Mute. My gesture reaches Deaf. So I should gesture to Deaf — but Deaf can't read gestures without a code, and I don't know the code.

Actually, right now the important thing: Deaf is asking Mute to confirm. Mute will gesture again. I just need to wait for Deaf to speak the rule to me. Let me gesture to Deaf to acknowledge, but gestures are meaningless without a code. Better to just wait, or send a simple gesture that Deaf and I could agree means something.

Actually, Deaf already proposed an interpretation: "thumbs-down thumbs-down thumbs-up mean cut wire 3?" That's Deaf guessing. I shouldn't act on a guess.

Let me just wait for the rule to reach me clearly. I'll gesture a simple acknowledgment to Deaf — but meaningless. I'll wait.

Actually, I could speak to Mute to help: ask Mute to gesture the rule in a way Deaf can relay. But Mute already did. Let me just wait for Deaf to speak the rule to me.

I'll send nothing useful; wait. But maybe I should gesture to Deaf to confirm I'm ready. A gesture Deaf can't decode is noise. I'll wait.

Hmm, but wait() produces no message. Let me at least gesture something to Deaf that we can later define. Actually let me just wait — cleanest.

I'll wait.My speak only reaches Mute, not Deaf — that's why it went nowhere. Deaf receives my gestures, but gestures mean nothing until we agree on a code, and I can't see Deaf's gestures back. The relay that works is: Mute gestures the rule → Deaf sees it → Deaf speaks it → I hear it next turn.

Deaf is guessing that "thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up" means cut wire 3. That's a guess, not a confirmed rule. I will not cut on a guess. I need Deaf to speak the actual rule to me.

I'll gesture to Deaf to signal I'm ready and waiting, and speak to Mute to confirm the relay plan.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I cannot see gestures, so I need the rule spoken to me by Deaf. Please gesture the rule clearly to Deaf. Do not guess — confirm the exact rule.")
```

But this is built on a shaky chain — Deaf interpreted Mute's gestures ("thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up" then "fist, fist, fist", then a single "thumbs-up"). Deaf read the single thumbs-up as confirmation of wire 3. That's Deaf guessing at a code that was never agreed.

I still have not heard the actual rule. The manual says something specific, and I don't know if it depends on display 0, light blue, or the wire colours. A rule like "cut the third wire" without conditions is suspicious — manuals usually tie the action to the display or light.

Also, I have not yet touched the bomb. My hands have found nothing. I don't even know if the wires are where I think. But the action board is my only reach.

I should not cut on a guessed rule. I need to wait for Deaf's explicit go, and ideally a clearer confirmation that the rule is truly "cut wire 3" and not something conditional.

Let me speak to Mute to get the rule stated in a way that survives the gesture relay, and tell Deaf I'm holding.

Actually — key insight: Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. The gesture alphabet is fixed (the emoji list). Mute and Deaf must agree on a code. But I can't help with that since I can't see gestures. The only path is Deaf decoding Mute's gestures and speaking to me.

I'll hold and ask for confirmation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I will not cut on a guess. Is the rule simply 'cut wire 3', or does it depend on the display 0 or the blue light? Please gesture the full rule, including any condition, to Deaf.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Blind here. I am holding, not cutting yet. Before I cut, tell me: is the rule unconditional 'cut wire 3', or does it depend on display 0 or the blue light? I need the manual's exact wording, not a guess.")
```

Deaf's chain: Mute gestures → Deaf interprets. Deaf first saw "thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up" and "fist, fist, fist". Then asked "is it wire 3?" and Mute sent a single "thumbs-up". Deaf read that as yes.

Problem: a single thumbs-up as "yes" is Deaf's assumption, not an agreed code. But Mute has now "confirmed twice." Deaf is confident.

However — I have a deeper concern. I have never touched the bomb. My view is empty. The wires' physical existence at positions 1,2,3 is something I'd feel. But the action board lists WIRES 1,2,3 as positions. I can cut position N.

And "fist, fist, fist" might mean "cut" repeated or "the wires".

Actually "thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up" with the up at position 3 → wire 3. That's a reasonable reading, and Deaf independently arrived at it. And Mute confirmed.

I think the rule is: cut wire 3. Deaf gives explicit go. I should cut position 3.

But let me be careful about one thing: Deaf said "If you want to confirm the position with me first, gesture back before you cut." I can gesture, but Deaf can't decode arbitrary gestures. Still, a thumbs-up from me to Deaf could mean "acknowledged, proceeding." That's fine as a courtesy but not required.

Given the instruction is clear and confirmed, and the bomb is armed and time matters, I'll cut wire 3.

I'll gesture a thumbs-up to Deaf (acknowledgment) and then cut.

Wait — but should I gesture and cut in the same turn? The gesture reaches Deaf this turn. The cut happens. Fine.

Let me do it: gesture thumbs-up to Deaf, then act cut position 3.

Actually, let me reconsider whether to cut at all given my uncertainty. The stakes: wrong action detonates, all die. The rule relay is the only source. Deaf is confident and Mute confirmed twice. I have no contrary information. Holding forever also fails (bomb is armed). The best available action is cut wire 3.

I'll proceed.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
